_note: Draft English rendering of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Devarim 16, generated by scripts/translate_tafsir_english.py against the JA (not the biblical Hebrew). Translation goal: reverse-translatability for the Tafsir reader — readers should be able to map English back to JA. Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: And observe the month of the ripening grain, that you make in it a Passover to God your Lord, as He released you in it, to go forth from Egypt by night.
translations.2: And slaughter the Passover to God your Lord — from the flock, and with it from the cattle — in the place which God shall choose, that He may let His light dwell therein.
translations.3: Do not eat leavened bread with it; rather, eat after it seven days unleavened bread — the food of the weak — for you went forth from Egypt in haste. And remember the day of your going forth from Egypt all the length of your time.
translations.4: And let no leaven be seen for you in all your territory seven days; and let none of the flesh which you slaughter in the evening remain until the morning of the first day.
translations.5: It is not permitted that you slaughter the Passover in any of your settlements which God your Lord is giving you.
translations.6: But only in the place which God your Lord shall choose, that He may let His light dwell therein — there you shall slaughter the Passover at the evening, before the setting of the sun; and that is at the season of your going forth from Egypt.
translations.7: And cook it and eat it in that place which God your Lord shall choose; then turn away in the morning, and go to your dwelling.
translations.8: And eat after it unleavened bread six days; and on the seventh day — an abiding in the holiness of God your Lord; you shall do no work therein.
translations.9: And count seven weeks, from the time the sickle begins among the ears of grain — begin the count.
translations.10: And make the festival of Weeks to God your Lord, according to the measure of what your hand attains and what you offer voluntarily, as God your Lord has provided for you.
translations.11: And rejoice before Him — you, and your son, and your daughter, and your manservant, and your maidservant, and the Levite who is in your settlements, and the stranger, and the orphan, and the widow who are in your midst — in the place which God your Lord shall choose, that He may let His light dwell therein.
translations.12: And remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and observe these statutes and act by them.
translations.13: And make the festival of Booths seven days, at the time of your gathering your harvest from your sowing and your produce.
translations.14: And rejoice at this festival of yours — you, and your son, and your daughter, and your manservant, and your maidservant, and the Levite, and the stranger, and the orphan, and the widow who are in your settlements.
translations.15: So shall you make pilgrimage seven days to God your Lord, in the place which He shall choose, so that God your Lord may bless you in all your harvest and the rest of what you put your hand to; and you shall be in wholly pure joy.
translations.16: Three times in the year all your men shall appear before God your Lord in the place which He shall choose — at the pilgrimage of unleavened bread, and the pilgrimage of Weeks, and the pilgrimage of Booths; and they shall not appear before Me empty-handed.
translations.17: But each man shall come according to what his hand attains, according to the provision of God your Lord which He has given you.
translations.18: And appoint for yourself judges and overseers in all your settlements which God your Lord gives to your tribes; and they shall judge among the people with a just judgment.
translations.19: Do not skew the judgment, and do not show partiality to persons, and do not take a bribe — for the bribe blinds the eyes of the learned to the truth, and corrupts words that are just.
translations.20: And pursue pure justice earnestly, so that you may live and possess the land which God your Lord is giving you.
translations.21: And do not plant for yourself a tree-pole beside the altar of God your Lord which you shall make.
translations.22: And do not erect for yourself a platform-stone — that which God your Lord abhors.
